tender.title: Independent Child Trafficking Guardianship (ICTG) Service
tender.description:
The Government is committed to tackling the terrible crime of modern slavery. The Modern Slavery Act (MSA) 2015 provides the legal framework for tackling modern slavery in the UK, it gives law enforcement agencies the tools to combat it and sets out our obligations to ensure victims are proactively identified and supported. Since the introduction of the MSA, the first legislation of its kind in the world, successive governments have continued to commit to tackling this crime. The National Referral Mechanism (NRM), a system for identifying and supporting potential victims of modern slavery towards independence, is also an integral part of the Government’s approach to supporting victims to recover and reduce risks of re-trafficking.
Modern Slavery encompasses slavery, servitude, forced and compulsory labour and human trafficking. Modern Slavery is often ‘hidden in plain sight’.
Traffickers and exploiters coerce, deceive and force individuals against their will into a life of abuse, servitude, and inhumane treatment. The exploitation can cause severe trauma and can leave victims with complex needs. In human trafficking cases, exploitation can take many forms, including sexual exploitation, forced labour, slavery, servitude, forced criminality and removal of organs.
The Independent Child Trafficking Guardianship (ICTG) Service has been running since 2017, initially in three sites, and now operating in two thirds of Local Authorities (LAs) in England and Wales. Through this Contract, the ICTG Service shall be expanded to cover all LAs in England & Wales.
Delivering the ICTG service is one way that the UK meets its domestic and legal obligations to Child Victims of Modern Slavery (CVoMS), alongside the statutory obligations on LAs to safeguard all children (including CVoMS) in their areas.
ICTGs provide an additional source of advice and support for potentially trafficked children, irrespective of nationality or immigration status, and somebody to advocate on their behalf to ensure their best interests are reflected in the decision-making of the Public Authorities involved in their care.
An ICTG’s advocacy and involvement throughout the decision-making process is intended to ensure the Child is protected from further harm, prevent possible repeat victimisation, re-trafficking or going missing, and promote the Child’s recovery.
The ICTG Service model provides one-to-one Direct Support for Children with no parental responsibility for them in the UK and Indirect Support for Children where there is someone with parental responsibility for them in the UK. In exceptional circumstances, Children with a Figure of Parental Responsibility (FOPR) for them in the UK can receive Direct Support.
Referrals into the ICTG Service are made by First Responders (FR) or First Responder Organisations (FRO).
The ICTG Service supports Children from the moment they enter the NRM process, providing independent, specialist guidance. If Children receive a Negative Reasonable Grounds Decision or Negative Conclusive Grounds Decision, Support will end, subject to the Reconsideration Requests process and Exit Criteria detailed in this Contract.
More information on the ICTG Service can be found in the Data Room, in the Jaggaer Portal following registration.

tender.description:
Description of Requirement 
The Ministry of Defence, acting through the British Forces Post Office (BFPO), intends to procure a comprehensive global mail conveyance service to support the delivery and return of Forces mail and courier services worldwide. 
BFPO's mission is to provide an efficient, effective and resilient postal and courier service in order to sustain the fighting power of UK Armed Forces worldwide. BFPO delivers postal services to Service Personnel, Defence Civil Servants and entitled family members located across the globe through a combination of military and commercial transportation networks.  
The Authority is considering a requirement that may include some or all of the following service elements: 
Scheduled Worldwide Mail Conveyance 
International inbound and outbound mail conveyance services. 
Freight forwarding through commercial air carriers and express courier networks. 
Customs management and associated documentation. 
Provision of tracking and tracing services. 
Non-Scheduled (Ad Hoc) Worldwide Mail Conveyance 
Urgent and operational mail movements. 
Support to HM Ships and deployed military operations. 
Flexible worldwide collection and delivery capability. 
Airport Road Trunking 
Routine movement of mail between BFPO Headquarters and designated airport cargo facilities. 
Handling, storage and secure transportation of military mail consignments. 
UK Road Trunking 
Collection and delivery services between BFPO, Royal Mail facilities, RAF Brize Norton and other Defence locations. 
Provision of suitable vehicles, drivers and associated operational support. 
Witness Loading and Specialist Freight Forwarding Services 
Support for secure international movement of designated consignments. 
Airport handling and customs liaison activities. 
Entry Summary Declaration (ENS) Filing Services 
Submission and management of customs declarations and associated regulatory requirements. 
Support for BFPO requirements relating to the movement of mail into EU territories.  
Key Requirements 
Potential suppliers should be capable of demonstrating: 
Proven experience in international freight forwarding, mail conveyance or logistics services. 
Access to worldwide transportation networks. 
Appropriate aviation, freight forwarding and customs accreditations. 
Robust track and trace capabilities. 
Ability to operate within secure and sensitive government environments. 
Compliance with all applicable UK transport, customs, security and health and safety legislation. 
Business continuity and resilience arrangements capable of supporting operational military requirements. 
Experience supporting public sector or defence customers is desirable.  
Market Engagement 
The Authority intends to undertake market engagement activities with interested suppliers prior to commencing the formal procurement. These activities may include Requests for Information (RFI), supplier engagement events, one-to-one discussions and industry briefings. 
Information gathered through market engagement will be used to inform the final procurement strategy, requirements, lotting structure and commercial approach. 
Participation in pre-market engagement activities will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. 
Procurement Act 2023 
The Authority intends to conduct any future procurement in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and associated regulations. 
Further information, including any Preliminary Market Engagement Notice (UK2), Tender Notice (UK4) and procurement documentation, will be published on the Central Digital Platform at the appropriate time. 
Additional Information 
This Pipeline Notice is issued for information and procurement planning purposes only and does not commit the Authority to commence any procurement or enter into any contractual arrangement. 
The scope, procurement timetable, contract structure and estimated value remain subject to business approvals, funding and further development of the requirement.

tender.title: West Midlands at MIPIM and UKREiiF 2027 Pavilion – Design & Fit Out
tender.description:
The real estate calendar is dominated by two large conferences, MIPIM and UKREiiF. Both events are critical to the West Midlands as key opportunities to market the region domestically and internationally, promote opportunities and announcements, and engage with an investor and developer audience.
MIPIM is a globally recognised real estate and investment event, held annually in Cannes, bringing together investors, developers, public sector leaders, and key decision-makers from across the global property and investment market.
Over recent years, WMGC has delivered the regional presence at MIPIM through a tactical model focused on targeted business development activity, stakeholder engagement and investor meetings. Whilst this approach has delivered positive outcomes, feedback from both public and private sector stakeholders has indicated that the model is approaching its natural limitations, and that a more visible and anchored presence is required to support investor engagement and regional promotion.
Following engagement with regional stakeholders, and consideration through governance channels, it has been agreed that WMGC will lead the delivery of an enhanced presence at MIPIM 2027.  
UKREiiF is the UK’s real estate investment and infrastructure forum. tender.description:
The London Borough of Hillingdon is looking for suitably qualified consultants to be party to a Framework Agreement for Building and Construction Consultancy Services.
The Scope of the Framework Agreement
The Framework will consist of the following Lots:
1.	Multi-Disciplinary Services
2.	Architectural and Building Design Services
3.	Building Services Engineering (M&E)
4.	Building Surveying Services
5.	Structural Engineering
6.	Quantity Surveying Services
7.	 Environmental and Sustainability Advisory
8.	Employers Agent
9.	CDM Principal Designer
10.	Building Safety Act Principal Designer
Above is a list of the Lots, if a requirement would fit under the Lot heading, it is considered included. Each Lot will include additional elements such as tender preparation, tendering, project management services, the provision of a wide range of advice on all matters concerned with planning, development and environmental issues which surround a building project.
Each Lot is also available as Multi-Disciplinary, providing the Lot selected at Call Off is the main requirement of the intended project.
This is a Competitive Flexible Procedure with 2 stages.
Stage 1 - (Selection Stage) will have the following weighting:
Quality (Technical)- 100%
It is intended that the Authority will shortlist to all those Applicants that are ranked within the top 10 of Stage 1 and to any that are tied 10th for each Lot and will then be invited to the second stage of the procurement process, the Invitation to Tender (ITT - Stage 2)
Those shortlisted and invited to tender under Stage 2 - (ITT) will be evaluated on the following weightings:
Commercial (Price) - 30%
Quality (Technical)- 70%
Each shortlisted Applicant will be invited at the ITT stage 2 to submit a tender.
Following the ITT Stage, the intention of the Framework Agreement is to Award places to the top 6 ranked bids and to any that are tied 6th, per Lot.
The maximum number of Lots that can be awarded to any one Consultant will be six (6) Lots.
At ITT stage, If a consultant is ranked within the top six scoring bids for more than six Lots, they will have Lots selected for them based upon their order of preference with the vacancy from the discarded Lots given to the next lower ranked consultant who has placed a bid in the discarded Lot. Where there are no other lower ranked Consultants, more than six Lots can be awarded.
Each Lot will be divided into Project Price Bands of the following amounts:
Project Price Band A  £0 - £50k
Project Price Band B  £50k - £250k
Project Price Band C  £250k - £750K
Project Price Band D  £750 - £2M
Project Price Band E  £2M - £5M
Project Price Band F  £5M - £10M
Project Price Band G  £10M - £20M
Any project that is above £20m in value will be subject to a Mini-Competition.
All bidders must return rates for all Price Bands within the Lot(s) they are applying for.
The fees submitted should be the maximum fees you are prepared to charge at Call Off Stage for a Direct Award.
It is expected that upon conclusion of the Framework Agreement it will be made available to other Nationwide Public Bodies, to utilise if they wish to do so via an Access Agreement.
Each Lot will be evaluated and awarded separately. Tenderers will need to complete all required sections within each Lot to be considered.
This is for a Framework with a duration of 4 years, available to any public body to use if they wish. There is no pipeline of projects available as we cannot anticipate its use.

Preliminary Market Engagement Notice (UK02)
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) intends to undertake a procurement exercise for the supply of Dimethyl Sulphoxide (DMSO) for use in the cryopreservation of stem cell and immunotherapy products across NHSBT Cellular and Molecular Therapies (CMT) laboratories. 
NHSBT is seeking to engage with suppliers and manufacturers of DMSO products to improve its understanding of available solutions within the market, identify innovation opportunities, assess supplier capability, and inform the development of the procurement and specification requirements ahead of any future tender exercise. 
Background
Cellular and Molecular Therapies (CMT), part of NHSBT's Cellular and Gene Therapies Directorate (CAGT), operates specialist laboratories located in Barnsley, Birmingham, Filton, Oxford and Southampton. These laboratories process, test, store and distribute cellular therapy products for transplantation and immunotherapy treatments. DMSO is used during the cryopreservation process to preserve cells during long-term storage at temperatures below -150°C. 
Requirement Overview
NHSBT is interested in obtaining information from suppliers capable of providing DMSO products that meet the following indicative requirements:
Technical Requirements
• Sterile liquid DMSO ready for use.
• Pyrogen-free product.
• Minimum purity of 99.9%.
• Compliance with current European and/or United States Pharmacopoeia standards.
• UKCA or CE marked where applicable.
• Availability in: 
o Vials or bottles (Lot 1); and/or
o Alternative containers such as bags or syringes suitable for sterile docking systems (Lot 2).
• Evidence that primary packaging materials are compatible with DMSO throughout the stated shelf life.
• Certificate of Analysis/Compliance supplied with each batch.
• Clear batch and expiry date labelling.
• Confirmation regarding DEHP content where applicable.
• Assurance that no animal-derived materials are used in manufacture and that there is no risk of cross-contamination. 
Supply and Service Requirements
• Ability to maintain contingency stock equivalent to at least three months' NHSBT demand.
• Guaranteed supply continuity and delivery performance.
• Minimum six months' shelf life remaining upon delivery.
• Agreement to quality audits where required.
• Business continuity arrangements suitable for the supply of critical healthcare consumables.
• Robust product recall, complaint handling and adverse event management procedures.
• Ability to replace unsatisfactory stock within 24 hours where necessary
Areas for Market Engagement
NHSBT would welcome discussions with suppliers regarding:
• Available DMSO products and packaging formats.
• Manufacturing and quality assurance arrangements.
• Supply chain resilience and continuity of supply.
• Shelf-life optimisation.
• Environmental sustainability initiatives.
• Future product developments and innovations.
• Market capacity and opportunities to improve value for money. 
Supplier Engagement
NHSBT intends to undertake preliminary market engagement activities between 24 August 2026 and 4 September 2026.
Engagement may take the form of:
• Virtual supplier meetings;
• Written questionnaires;
• Product presentations or demonstrations;
• Technical discussions; and/or
• Requests for further product and market information.
To enable NHSBT to finalise arrangements, interested organisations are requested to submit an expression of interest by email to sahithi.bandi@nhsbt.nhs.uk no later than 17:00 BST on 21 August 2026.
Expressions of interest should include:
• Organisation name.
• Contact details.
• Proposed attendees.
• Brief overview of relevant products and services.
• Product literature and/or company capability information.
Participation in this preliminary market engagement exercise will not influence any future procurement process and will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any subsequent competition. Information obtained during the engagement will be used solely to support NHSBT in developing its procurement strategy and refining its requirements. 
Important Information
This notice is issued solely for the purpose of preliminary market engagement under the Procurement Act 2023.
No business whatsoever is guaranteed under any resulting contract or framework agreement, and there is no guarantee that a procurement process will be commenced following this notice. No compensation or reimbursement of costs will be paid to organisations participating in this market engagement exercise. Organisations participate entirely at their own cost and risk. 
NHSBT reserves the right not to proceed with any procurement process following completion of the engagement activities.
Any future procurement may be available for use by NHS Blood and Transplant and other eligible contracting authorities where permitted. [Sample of...PIN draft | Word]

milestones.description:
NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board, Bristol City Council, North Somerset Council and South Gloucestershire Council ("the Commissioners") are responsible for commissioning health and care services for children, young people and families across Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG).
The Commissioners are commencing a programme of market engagement to help inform future commissioning arrangements for community-based children's and young people's health services across BNSSG.
The Commissioners are currently reviewing how community children's services are commissioned and delivered across the system to ensure that future arrangements continue to meet the needs of children, young people and families, support improved outcomes, and deliver high-quality, integrated services.
At this stage, no decisions have been made regarding the future scope of services, commissioning approach, service delivery model, contract structure, procurement process, or Provider Selection Regime (PSR) pathway. The Commissioners are therefore seeking early engagement with the market to understand provider perspectives, innovation, capability and capacity across the sector.
Purpose of the Market Engagement
This market engagement is intended to:
•	Inform the market of the Commissioners' review of community children's services across BNSSG
•	Seek feedback and insight from providers on proposed modelling, opportunities, challenges and priorities for future service delivery
•	To enable potential bidders to understand the potential capabilities, experience and capacity of organisations that may be required in the delivery of community children's services
•	Begin to explore the transformation journey and the potential for collaborative approaches in delivering integrated care for children, young people and families over the contract period
•	Gather any further information that may help shape the commissioning intent, service models and procurement approaches
•	Support transparent, fair and proportionate decision-making in accordance with the Provider Selection Regime
Feedback received through this engagement process will be used to help inform the Commissioners' strategic thinking and modelling. To reiterate, no decisions have yet been made regarding the procurement or commissioning approach. All options remain under consideration.
Scope of Engagement
The Commissioners are interested in obtaining views from organisations with experience of delivering, supporting or partnering in the provision of community children's health services and related services for children, young people and families.
The engagement is intended to be broad in scope and may cover areas including, but not limited to:
•	Community-based health services for children and young people
•	Integrated and multidisciplinary models of care
•	Prevention and early intervention approaches
•	How the services may support children and young people with additional needs, disabilities or long-term conditions
•	Collaboration between health, local authority, and other stakeholders
•	Workforce, digital and service transformation opportunities
•	Approaches to improving access, outcomes and experience for children, young people and families
The Commissioners are seeking to start the market engagement with a virtual (MS TEAMS) event that is due to take place on Wednesday 9th September 2026. It is intended that future events will take place, these may be held either virtually or face to face. 
Participation is voluntary and open to all interested providers, including NHS, independent sector, voluntary sector, and partnerships/consortia.
Interested providers will be able to view this opportunity via the live opportunities list on the 'Health Family' e-procurement system, Atamis. Click on 'View our Live Opportunities' from the home page, available on the following link: https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome. 
Once you have found the opportunity (via the search function, using the title or reference number: C462766 ), to gain full access you will need to click on 'Register interest' - this will take you to the log-in page. You MUST complete your registration for this event via the Microsoft Forms application via this opportunity.

tender.title: Woolwich Ferry Linkspan Maintenance
tender.description:
Transport for London (TfL) are looking to explore the market to establish the interest and appetite for suppliers to deliver maintenance service to Woolwich Ferry (WF) Linkspan systems. The linkspans at the south and north terminals provide the means of access and egress for all ferry passengers, therefore the reliability of them is critical to achieving good service performance. 
The service includes planning, design and delivery of cyclic maintenance of the linkspans in accordance with the requirements of the Operation and Maintenance Manual and to ensure that the assets perform reliably in meeting the demands of the WF service. The service will also include supply and installation activities. 
There are four Linkspans that provide a drawbridge for vehicles and pedestrians to access and egress the Woolwich Ferry. The scope of this procurement (including options) allows for: 
- Undertaking Linkspan maintenance activities that are required every 5 years (replacement of key components)
- 3 month, 6 month, 12 month and 24-monthly cyclic maintenance activities (specialist inspection and testing of Linkspan lifting and span systems)
- Reactive maintenance (technical support, call out and repair)

The Supplier shall be responsible for the design, supply, installation, management, and ongoing maintenance of EV charging equipment and associated infrastructure. The scope of the project includes both the new charging units and, upon contract expiry (01 September 2027), the ongoing management and maintenance of the four (4) existing dual-socket units, with the objective of delivering a single, cohesive solution across the campus.
All EV charging infrastructure forming part of this Contract, shall be installed within University owned private car parks at the Egham campus.
The University reserves the right to instruct the Supplier to undertake additional, related Services that support the successful purchase, installation, commissioning, operation, servicing and maintenance of EV Charging Points, where such Services remain consistent with the nature, scale and purpose of the Contract. These additional requirements may include, but are not limited to: 
A) Additional site surveys, feasibility assessments, electrical capacity analysis or design development required to support the installation or expansion of EV Charging Points.
B) Further installation, commissioning or configuration of EV Charging Points arising from changes to site layouts, usage demand or University requirements.

tender.title: Department for Transport Shared Research, Evaluation and Analysis
tender.description:
The Department for Transport (DfT) is considering procuring a shared research, evaluation and analysis call-off contract to provide flexible access to timely, high-quality research, monitoring, evaluation, economic analysis and related analytical support across a range of transport policy areas. The proposed contract is expected to support analytical requirements across four divisions, which cover a broad range of transport policy areas:  
Accessible and inclusive transport (particular focus on those with physical and mental health conditions and/or groups with different protected characteristics) 
Active travel (cycling, wheeling and walking) 
Buses, planning and housing 
Devolution of responsibility for transport in England, including devolution deals, place-based policy, and strategy for integrated transport 
Local highways maintenance 
Local Authority capability and capacity 
Passenger transport (light rail, taxis, private hire vehicles, community transport) 
Road Freight (including: roadworthiness and vehicle regulation; international freight; HGV driver skills, hours and working conditions; traffic commissioners and operator licencing) 
Multimodal Freight (including: modal shift; freight innovation funding; work to improve connectivity of data and insights across the freight network) 
Dangerous Goods 
Future Borders (including policies to improve traffic management in Kent) 
Borders Resilience and Response (managing disruption at borders and along the strategic road network) 
Road safety (including supporting road users, safer vehicles, post collision care, safer infrastructure, and enforcement) 
Motoring Agencies (DVSA, DVLA and VCA – including MOT and driver licensing) 
International Vehicle Standards 
Connected and Autonomous vehicles 
AI, data, and other emerging transport technologies 
Vehicle Infrastructure (e.g. charging) 
Strategic Roads (Strategic Road Network managed by National Highways) 
Traffic and Technology (including traffic management, parking, street works etc.) 
Micro-mobility, such as e-scooters, and other forms of transport innovation (e.g. pavement robots) 
Lower Thames Crossing  
These divisions are home to more than 80 analysts with expertise in social research, evaluation, behavioural science, economics, operational research, statistics, and transport modelling; any of whom could commission work through the contract during its lifetime.  
The proposed contract would replace and expand the remit of an existing call-off contract that commenced in March 2023. The current draft requirement is for a call-off contract under which up to three suppliers may be appointed and individual commissions would be agreed as requirements arise. The current draft maximum budget is £6,000,000 excluding VAT. The proposed contract term is February 2027 to February 2031, or until the budget is exhausted, whichever is sooner. Commissions agreed before the contract end date may continue, provided each commission is completed within seven years of its start date. 
The proposed contract is expected to cover a broad range of research, evaluation, economic analysis and related analytical services. This may include, but is not limited to: evidence reviews and synthesis; qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods primary research; secondary analysis of existing datasets; advanced quantitative analysis, modelling and forecasting; behavioural, user-centred and accessibility-focused research; monitoring and evaluation, including process, impact, outcome and value for money evaluation; cost-benefit analysis, economic appraisal and economic evaluation; and analytical quality assurance. 
Suppliers would be expected to demonstrate broad analytical capability and be able to design, deliver, peer review, quality assure and clearly communicate high-quality, policy-relevant analysis in line with relevant government guidance, including the Magenta Book, Green Book and AQuA Book. Across all work, suppliers will be expected to apply proportionate methods, document assumptions and limitations clearly, and translate findings into practical recommendations for policy, operational or funding decisions. 
Suppliers would be expected to provide sufficient technical expertise, capacity, resilience and project management capability to deliver multiple commissions concurrently, including short-term, medium-term and longer-term projects of varying complexity. Suppliers may deliver requirements through their own organisation, consortium arrangements, named subcontractors or other approved delivery partners. Due to the broad nature of the proposed requirements, the Department encourages suppliers to consider whether consortium, subcontracting or other partnership arrangements would help them provide the necessary breadth of expertise, capacity and resilience. Any such arrangements should include clear lines of responsibility, with the lead supplier retaining appropriate oversight and accountability for quality, timeliness, confidentiality, continuity and management of all work delivered under the contract. 
Outputs from the proposed contract would be used to inform policy and operational decisions and to build the evidence base across a range of transport policy areas. Outputs may include, depending on the individual commission, reports, slide packs, spreadsheets, datasets, analytical code, models, evidence logs, technical annexes and other supporting materials. The DfT expects outputs to be robust, proportionate, clearly communicated, appropriately documented, quality assured and suitable for policy, analytical and, where relevant, public audiences. 
Individual commissions are expected to have tailored milestones, deliverables and outputs. Suppliers may be expected to provide sufficient documentation to enable the Department to understand, review, use and, where appropriate, update or reuse outputs in future.  
The DfT expects that any future contract will include requirements on the safe, transparent and proportionate use of AI, including generative AI, machine learning and AI-enabled tools used to support research, evaluation or analysis. Supplier views may be sought through preliminary market engagement on how AI can be used responsibly while managing data protection, security, ethics, transparency, bias and quality risks. 
The information provided in this notice is indicative and non-binding. The scope, value, timetable, procurement approach, contract structure and requirements may be refined following preliminary market engagement and internal approvals.

tender.title: St George's RC Primary School SUDS in Schools Scheme
tender.description:
St Georges Primary School is located in Lemington, north of Scotswood Road and the northern bank of the River Tyne. The school is located ~30m east of Sugley Dene Burn and has suffered repeated internal flooding due to surface water ingress during high intensity storms, in part due to its location on the flow route of a steep, sloping topography with natural overland flows heading towards the River Tyne. 
NaFRA2 maps indicated that the school is at risk in a 1 in 100-year event, however the local topography and reported flooding from the school mean this is likely to be a conservative estimate of risk. Currently, surface water is managed by a private drainage system comprising of roof drainage, storm drains and channel drains located in front of the main entrance to the building, which is four steps lower than the yard / hardstanding area around it. These drainage features are easily overwhelmed in heavy storms and surface water enters the school buildings. Maintenance of these components is undertaken by the school caretaker. 
The project will intercept and attenuate surface water in SuDS features before discharge back into the school's private drainage.
SuDS in Schools is a fund established by the Department for Education (DfE) to improve the resilience of schools to flooding issues by implementing Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS). The LLFA applied for funding and was informed it had been successful in 2025. DfE funding is for a maximum of 50% of any project. The Northumbria Regional Flood & Coast Committee has subsequently agreed to match fund the other 50% of successful DfE bids.
It is only practicable to undertake SuDS in Schools projects during the summer holidays, given the timescales involved in the construction of these projects and the need to minimize disruption to the school and safety issues for staff and pupils.
SuDS projects aim to manage storm water when conventional drainage systems are overwhelmed. Surface water is stored or "attenuated" in features like basins, swales or raingardens, which then slowly release water back into the environment once the peak of a storm has passed. As well reducing flood risk, features should be designed to deliver environmental, health and wellbeing and amenity benefits.
